article_title: Cognitive Architecture and Instructional Design: 20 Years Later
citation: Sweller, J., van Merriënboer, J. J. G., & Paas, F. (2019). Cognitive Architecture and Instructional Design: 20 Years Later. Educational Psychology Review, 31, 261–292. https://doi.org/10.1007/s10648-019-09465-5
title: 4C/ID model extends cognitive load theory to course and curriculum design through four components
description: The four-component instructional design (4C/ID) model, developed in parallel with CLT on the same cognitive architecture, designs whole courses for complex learning with high element interactivity. The article states that "The 4C/ID model provides an important extension to cognitive load theory because it focuses on the design of educational programs of longer duration (e.g. courses or whole curricula)." Its four components are learning tasks, supportive information, procedural information, and part-task practice, managing intrinsic, extraneous and germane load respectively.
requirements: Learning tasks organised in increasing complexity levels with fading support; supportive information presented apart from task performance; procedural information presented just-in-time
constraints: The model exclusively deals with complex learning; over-reliance on part-task practice is not helpful for complex learning
target_learners: learners in longer educational programs developing complex skills or professional competencies
target_learning_goals: coordination of recurrent and non-recurrent constituent skills; knowledge automation
examples: Learning tasks are sequenced as a spiral curriculum with diminishing guidance, using the completion strategy from worked examples via completion tasks to conventional tasks
key_sources: Sweller, J., van Merriënboer, J. J. G., & Paas, F. (2019). Cognitive Architecture and Instructional Design: 20 Years Later. Educational Psychology Review, 31, 261–292. https://doi.org/10.1007/s10648-019-09465-5

citation: van Merriënboer, J.J.G., Clark, R.E. & de Croock, M.B.M. (2002). Blueprints for complex learning: The 4C/ID-model. ETR&D. https://doi.org/10.1007/BF02504993
title: The 4C/ID-model: a four-component instructional design system for training complex skills
description: The article describes the four-component instructional design system (4C/ID-model), developed originally by van Merriënboer and others in the early 1990s for the design of training programs for complex skills. The model structures training blueprints for complex learning around four interrelated components and specifies instructional methods for each component coupled to the basic learning processes involved in complex learning. The article presents the model's blueprint structure and illustrates it with a worked-out example.
requirements: Designers must produce training blueprints for complex learning that include all four interrelated components
constraints: The model was developed for the design of training programs for complex skills
examples: A fully worked-out example of a training blueprint for searching for literature is provided in the article
key_sources: van Merriënboer, J.J.G., Clark, R.E. & de Croock, M.B.M. (2002). Blueprints for complex learning: The 4C/ID-model. ETR&D. https://doi.org/10.1007/BF02504993

citation: van Merriënboer, J.J.G., Clark, R.E. & de Croock, M.B.M. (2002). Blueprints for complex learning: The 4C/ID-model. ETR&D. https://doi.org/10.1007/BF02504993
title: Worked-out training blueprint for searching for literature
description: The article provides "a fully worked-out example of a training blueprint for 'searching for literature'" as a concrete instantiation of the 4C/ID-model. The blueprint demonstrates how the four components and their associated instructional methods are arranged in an actual training design for a complex skill, serving as a model designers can study when constructing their own blueprints.
requirements: Must be read alongside the four-component blueprint structure to serve as a design exemplar
constraints: The worked example targets the domain of searching for literature
target_learning_goals: literature searching as a complex skill
key_sources: van Merriënboer, J.J.G., Clark, R.E. & de Croock, M.B.M. (2002). Blueprints for complex learning: The 4C/ID-model. ETR&D. https://doi.org/10.1007/BF02504993

article_title: The Four-Component Instructional Design Model : Multimedia Principles in Environments for Complex Learning
citation: Jeroen J. G. van Merriënboer and Liesbeth Kester. (2005). The Four-Component Instructional Design Model : Multimedia Principles in Environments for Complex Learning. The Cambridge Handbook of Multimedia Learning, pp. 71-94. https://doi.org/10.1017/CBO9780511816819.006
title: The 4C-ID model claims four components are necessary to realize complex learning
description: The chapter presents the Four-Component Instructional Design (4C-ID) model as a framework for designing environments for complex learning. As the abstract states, "The Four-Component Instructional Design (4C-ID) model claims that four components are necessary to realize complex learning: (1) learning tasks, (2) supportive information, (3) procedural information, and (4) part-task practice." The chapter uses this framework to organize multimedia design guidance, relating multimedia principles to each of the four components.
requirements: Instruction for complex learning must include learning tasks, supportive information, procedural information, and part-task practice as distinct components
target_learning_goals: Complex learning integrating multiple knowledge and skill components
key_sources: Jeroen J. G. van Merriënboer and Liesbeth Kester. (2005). The Four-Component Instructional Design Model : Multimedia Principles in Environments for Complex Learning. The Cambridge Handbook of Multimedia Learning, pp. 71-94. https://doi.org/10.1017/CBO9780511816819.006

article_title: The Four-Component Instructional Design Model : Multimedia Principles in Environments for Complex Learning
citation: Jeroen J. G. van Merriënboer and Liesbeth Kester. (2005). The Four-Component Instructional Design Model : Multimedia Principles in Environments for Complex Learning. The Cambridge Handbook of Multimedia Learning, pp. 71-94. https://doi.org/10.1017/CBO9780511816819.006
title: Four learning processes are each facilitated by multimedia principles tied to one 4C-ID component
description: The chapter organizes 14 multimedia principles by mapping each of the four 4C-ID components to a distinct learning process and a matching multimedia environment. The abstract states the chapter "relates 14 multimedia principles to each of the four components," with inductive learning for learning tasks, elaboration and mindful abstraction for supportive information, knowledge compilation for procedural information, and psychological strengthening for part-task practice.
requirements: Multimedia principles must be selected to match the learning process each component is intended to facilitate
constraints: The framework is presented for design of multimedia learning environments; research implications and limitations are discussed in the chapter
target_learning_goals: Complex skill acquisition through coordinated multimedia environments
key_sources: Jeroen J. G. van Merriënboer and Liesbeth Kester. (2005). The Four-Component Instructional Design Model : Multimedia Principles in Environments for Complex Learning. The Cambridge Handbook of Multimedia Learning, pp. 71-94. https://doi.org/10.1017/CBO9780511816819.006

article_title: Cognitive Load Theory and Complex Learning: Recent Developments and Future Directions
citation: van Merriënboer, J.J.G., Sweller, J. (2005). Cognitive Load Theory and Complex Learning: Recent Developments and Future Directions. Educ Psychol Rev 17, 147–177 (2005). https://doi.org/10.1007/s10648-005-3951-0
title: 4C/ID model as a blueprint for complex learning
description: The 4C/ID model, authored by the first author of this review, is cited in the article's reference list as "Blueprints for complex learning: The 4C/ID-model" (van Merriënboer, Clark, and de Croock, 2002a). It represents a blueprint approach to designing complex learning consistent with the review's real-life-task perspective on managing high intrinsic load in complex skill acquisition.
requirements: Design of whole-task learning consistent with the real-life-tasks perspective on complex learning
key_sources: van Merriënboer, J.J.G., Sweller, J. (2005). Cognitive Load Theory and Complex Learning: Recent Developments and Future Directions. Educ Psychol Rev 17, 147–177 (2005). https://doi.org/10.1007/s10648-005-3951-0

article_title: Coaching effectiveness: the coach–athlete relationship at its heart
citation: Jowett, S. (2017). Coaching Effectiveness: The Coach-Athlete Relationship at its Heart. Current Opinion in Psychology, 16, 154-158. http://dx.doi.org/10.1016/j.copsyc.2017.05.006
title: The 4Cs operational model of coach-athlete relationship quality
description: The article describes the 4Cs model, which gives operational meaning to the quality of the coach-athlete relationship. It comprises closeness, reflecting an affective bond through mutual respect, trust, appreciation and liking; commitment, reflecting thoughts of maintaining a close relationship over time; complementarity, reflecting interpersonal behaviours of leadership and co-operation; and co-orientation, reflecting interdependence in views of the relationship. The review positions this quality as a medium allowing coaches and athletes to express wishes and fulfil ambitions, and as a barometer of coaching effectiveness.
requirements: Measurement of the quality dimensions requires validated instruments; the review notes that development and validation of Coach-Athlete Relationship Questionnaires facilitated the measurement of closeness, commitment and complementarity
target_learning_goals: performance and wellbeing of athletes and coaches
examples: The review cites a series of qualitative studies exploring content and functions of successful and less successful relationships, operationalised through the 4Cs
key_sources: Jowett, S. (2017). Coaching Effectiveness: The Coach-Athlete Relationship at its Heart. Current Opinion in Psychology, 16, 154-158. http://dx.doi.org/10.1016/j.copsyc.2017.05.006

article_title: Ten steps to 4C/ID: training differentiation skills in a professional development program for teachers
citation: Frerejean, J., van Geel, M., Keuning, T., Dolmans, D., van Merriënboer, J. J. G., & Visscher, A. J. (2021). Ten steps to 4C/ID: training differentiation skills in a professional development program for teachers. Instructional Science. https://doi.org/10.1007/s11251-021-09540-x
title: 4C/ID model: four components stimulating four essential learning processes for complex learning
description: The Four-Component Instructional Design model holds that educational programs for complex skills are described using four components: learning tasks, supportive information, procedural information, and part-task practice. Each component stimulates a learning process: inductive learning, elaboration, rule formation, and strengthening. The article states that "The 4C/ID model states that educational programs can be described using four components: a backbone of learning tasks based on authentic professional tasks, supportive information describing how to approach the tasks and how the domain is organized, procedural information describing step-by-step procedures to perform routine aspects of the tasks, and part-task practice for repetition of aspects that need to be highly automated." The design team applied this model to structure a teacher PD program.
requirements: Requires analysis of the complex skill to identify nonroutine and routine aspects before components can be designed
constraints: Intended for complex skills requiring integration of knowledge, skills, and attitudes and coordination of constituent skills
target_learning_goals: providing differentiated instruction in mathematics lessons
examples: The design team used 4C/ID to blueprint a five-month PD program for differentiation skills
key_sources: Frerejean, J., van Geel, M., Keuning, T., Dolmans, D., van Merriënboer, J. J. G., & Visscher, A. J. (2021). Ten steps to 4C/ID: training differentiation skills in a professional development program for teachers. Instructional Science. https://doi.org/10.1007/s11251-021-09540-x

article_title: Uniting epistemological perspectives to support contextualized knowledge development
citation: Sara van der Linden, Susan McKenney. (2020). Uniting epistemological perspectives to support contextualized knowledge development. Education Tech Research Dev. https://doi.org/10.1007/s11423-020-09772-7
title: 4C/ID as the underlying instructional design model for video coaching
description: The article positions the Four Components Instructional Design model as well-suited to the complex learning of united reflection during video coaching. It states this holistic approach "has been shown to stimulate the integration of knowledge, skills and attitudes", mitigating compartmentalization of learning tasks or fragmentation of constituent skills. The four components applied are whole learning tasks (RoA, RfA, RiA as task classes of increasing complexity), procedural information (the three reflection steps), supportive information, and part-task practice.
requirements: Authentic learning tasks that increase in complexity and are meaningful to learners
Procedural information to automate recurrent aspects of reflection
Supportive information bridging what learners know and need to know
target_learners: Early career teachers in video coaching programs
target_learning_goals: Complex learning integrating reflection perspectives and applying insights to practice
examples: RoA is classified as least complex, RfA medium complex, and RiA most complex because it combines all cognitive processes in the moment
key_sources: Sara van der Linden, Susan McKenney. (2020). Uniting epistemological perspectives to support contextualized knowledge development. Education Tech Research Dev. https://doi.org/10.1007/s11423-020-09772-7

article_title: Using Alice Software with 4C-ID Model: Effects in Programming Knowledge and Logical Reasoning
citation: Joana Martinho COSTA, Guilhermina Lobato MIRANDA. (2019). Using Alice Software with 4C-ID Model: Effects in Programming Knowledge and Logical Reasoning. Informatics in Education, 18(1), 1-15. https://doi.org/10.15388/infedu.2019.01
title: Four-Component Instructional Design (4C-ID) model for complex learning
description: The 4C-ID model, developed by van Merriënboer in the late 1990s, is an instructional design framework for acquiring complex learning, defined as integrating knowledge, skills and attitudes in a domain. It assumes knowledge is stored in cognitive schemes, working memory is limited and long-term memory effectively unlimited, and holds that "the learning tasks based on situations of the real life are the ones that enhance learning". It comprises four interrelated components: learning tasks, supportive information, procedural information, and part-task practice. In this article the model structured a set of Alice-based programming lessons, and the authors integrate Mayer's multimedia learning theory and Sweller's cognitive load theory into it.
requirements: Learning tasks must be based on real-life situations and require integration of logical reasoning and problem solving
Procedural information must be provided in small parts and only when the student needs it during task execution
constraints: Part-task practice is only used when the learning tasks don't present enough repetition
target_learners: secondary education students without previous programming experience
examples: The article's ten-week intervention used tutorial worksheets describing simulated problems, individualized cognitive feedback, progressive reduction of teacher support, and a final free-theme short-film challenge in Alice.
key_sources: Joana Martinho COSTA, Guilhermina Lobato MIRANDA. (2019). Using Alice Software with 4C-ID Model: Effects in Programming Knowledge and Logical Reasoning. Informatics in Education, 18(1), 1-15. https://doi.org/10.15388/infedu.2019.01

article_title: Using Alice Software with 4C-ID Model: Effects in Programming Knowledge and Logical Reasoning
citation: Joana Martinho COSTA, Guilhermina Lobato MIRANDA. (2019). Using Alice Software with 4C-ID Model: Effects in Programming Knowledge and Logical Reasoning. Informatics in Education, 18(1), 1-15. https://doi.org/10.15388/infedu.2019.01
title: Use the 4C-ID model in schools to minimize differences between students and promote academic and social integration
description: Based on their finding that the lower-SES, higher-retention group achieved a numerically superior covariate-adjusted programming average without a significant difference from the control group, the authors recommend broader school use of the model: "the use of the 4C-ID model should be more present in schools, since it minimizes the differences between the students and consequently promotes their academic and social integration." The recommendation rests on a small-sample quasi-experiment and is framed by the authors as a belief the results lead them to.
requirements: Instructional environments designed according to the four interrelated 4C-ID components
constraints: The small number of subjects in the supporting study does not allow generalization of the conclusions
target_learners: secondary education students from different socioeconomic backgrounds
target_learning_goals: academic achievement in complex skills such as programming
examples: The authors propose future work testing the 4C-ID model with other programming tools and other microworlds such as Scratch or StarLogo using the same instruments.
key_sources: Joana Martinho COSTA, Guilhermina Lobato MIRANDA. (2019). Using Alice Software with 4C-ID Model: Effects in Programming Knowledge and Logical Reasoning. Informatics in Education, 18(1), 1-15. https://doi.org/10.15388/infedu.2019.01

article_title: The 4C/ID-Model in Physics Education: Instructional Design of a Digital Learning Environment to Teach Electrical Circuits
citation: Melo, M. (2018). The 4C/ID-Model in Physics Education: Instructional Design of a Digital Learning Environment to Teach Electrical Circuits. International Journal of Instruction, 11(1), 103-122. https://doi.org/10.12973/iji.2018.1118a
title: The 4C/ID model: four interrelated blueprint components for complex learning
description: The 4C/ID model holds that settings for complex learning are described by four interrelated blueprint components: learning tasks (authentic whole tasks ordered easy-to-difficult with diminishing support), supportive information bridging prior and needed knowledge, just-in-time procedural information, and part-task practice for automaticity of routine aspects. The article states that "settings for complex learning can always be described by four interrelated blueprint components" and applies the model to design a 9th-grade electrical circuits environment. It rests on Cognitive Load Theory and Mayer's Multimedia Learning Theory.
requirements: Learning tasks must confront learners with all or almost all constituent skills, ordered from easy-to-difficult with support and guidance given when needed
constraints: Designing, developing, implementing and evaluating a learning environment according to this model is not an easy task and requires various types of conceptual and technical knowledge
target_learning_goals: Integrated complex skills such as analysing a simple electrical circuit, integrating knowledge, skills and attitudes
examples: The article decomposed the skill 'Analyse a simple electrical circuit' into a hierarchy of constituent skills and built three lessons with modeling examples, completion problems, conventional problems and part-task practice
key_sources: Melo, M. (2018). The 4C/ID-Model in Physics Education: Instructional Design of a Digital Learning Environment to Teach Electrical Circuits. International Journal of Instruction, 11(1), 103-122. https://doi.org/10.12973/iji.2018.1118a

article_title: The 4C/ID-Model in Physics Education: Instructional Design of a Digital Learning Environment to Teach Electrical Circuits
citation: Melo, M. (2018). The 4C/ID-Model in Physics Education: Instructional Design of a Digital Learning Environment to Teach Electrical Circuits. International Journal of Instruction, 11(1), 103-122. https://doi.org/10.12973/iji.2018.1118a
title: Six 4C/ID strategies for managing intrinsic, extraneous and germane cognitive load in whole-task instruction
description: The article lists six task-sequencing and information-presentation strategies the 4C/ID model suggests for managing cognitive load: sequencing task classes simple-to-complex, fading support from high to none, sequencing tasks in variable order (high contextual interference), presenting supportive information before and during whole-task practice, presenting just-in-time information when needed to prevent split-attention, and part-task practice to automate recurrent skills. It states "The 4C/ID-model suggests the following strategies, in terms of task sequencing and information presentation, to manage these types of cognitive load". The three load types are additive and cannot exceed working-memory capacity.
requirements: A well-designed instruction should optimize germane cognitive load within the limits of the total available working-memory capacity
constraints: Due to the task complexity of whole-task practices, students may have difficulties with learning, so cognitive load management is essential
target_learners: Novice learners of complex skills, here 9th-grade physics students
target_learning_goals: Schema construction and transfer in complex learning tasks
examples: In the electrical circuits environment, circuit complexity increased by introducing more elements connected in different forms, and tasks faded from modeling examples to completion problems to conventional problems
key_sources: Melo, M. (2018). The 4C/ID-Model in Physics Education: Instructional Design of a Digital Learning Environment to Teach Electrical Circuits. International Journal of Instruction, 11(1), 103-122. https://doi.org/10.12973/iji.2018.1118a

article_title: Covert audio recording of the clinical encounter to identify learning needs and exemplary performance in a pediatrics residency program.
citation: Salehi J, Schwartz A, Weiner SJ. (2026). Covert audio recording of the clinical encounter to identify learning needs and exemplary performance in a pediatrics residency program. PLOS One. https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pone.0344904
title: Content Coding for Contextualization of Care (4C) audio coding system
description: The 4C system is an audio coding framework for assessing how clinicians adapt care to patient circumstances. It "tracks four elements of physician-patient interaction": the contextual red flag, the contextual probe, the contextual factor, and the contextualized care plan. In this study a trained pediatrician coded covert recordings with 4C, supplemented by expert documentation of learning opportunities outside the framework.
requirements: Requires trained 4C coders; the article notes the coder was trained and validated by an experienced 4C trainer before coding.
constraints: The article states the process "remains resource-intensive," though ongoing work to automate 4C coding through artificial intelligence may reduce this burden.
target_learning_goals: contextualizing care — adapting care plans to patients' circumstances and behaviors
examples: Coding of 51 covertly recorded pediatric visits identified 50 contextual red flags, 6 probes, 8 contextual factors, and 2 contextualized care plans.
key_sources: Salehi J, Schwartz A, Weiner SJ. (2026). Covert audio recording of the clinical encounter to identify learning needs and exemplary performance in a pediatrics residency program. PLOS One. https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pone.0344904

article_title: Residency training for minimally invasive surgery.
citation: Campos MEC, Monteiro MVC, Kakehasi FM. (2022). Residency training for minimally invasive surgery. Revista do Colégio Brasileiro de Cirurgiões. https://doi.org/10.1590/0100-6991e-20213040
title: The 4C/ID model's four components as an instructional design model applied to surgical simulation training
description: The article describes the 4C/ID instructional design model with four components: "(1) learning task, which is the problem to be solved; (2) supportive information, which is the theory to solve the problem; (3) Just-In-Time (JIT) information, which are guidelines on how to solve the problem at the exact moment the learner needs it; and (4) part-task practice, which is the repeated training of parts of the task until the problem is solved as a whole." The authors state that all these instructional principles were included in their training program, citing JIT tutor support during practice.
requirements: Repeated part-task practice until the whole task is solved, per the model's fourth component
target_learners: surgical residents learning complex operative skills
examples: A tutor was present to assist the learner in time of need, described as Just In Time information; residents only advanced to the next exercise after reaching the previous exercise's goal.
key_sources: Campos MEC, Monteiro MVC, Kakehasi FM. (2022). Residency training for minimally invasive surgery. Revista do Colégio Brasileiro de Cirurgiões. https://doi.org/10.1590/0100-6991e-20213040
